title: Experimental prefill handoff policy and acceptance telemetry for speculative decode
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement an experimental runtime component that performs lightweight prefill probes, scores model candidates with a kernel-aware acceptance heuristic, and executes a safe fallback policy for speculative decode paths. Primary goal is to reduce tail latency for common short-response queries while keeping cost/regression risk bounded. This ticket covers the policy design, telemetry surface, a small prototype in the serving runtime, and an operational runbook for rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Probe mechanism produces <1ms additional median per-request overhead for cases that stay on fast-path
Acceptance heuristic achieves >= 95% agreement with ground-truth decode within first 4 tokens on held-out prompt set
Fallback path (quantized small model or dedicated slow pool) is exercised automatically when acceptance confidence < threshold and stays stable under load
Telemetry dashboard shows per-model acceptance rate, early-divergence frequency, probe cost delta, and SLA impact
Canary rollout hooks and abort criteria implemented in Console for runtime-1.20
implementation_notes: Probe budget: 2-4 prefill tokens sampled deterministically from prefix hash to avoid cache pollution
Scoring: combine token-level KL surrogate, kernel-affinity penalty (prefers kernels with low launch cost), and recent acceptance history using EWMA
Dynamic threshold: start with conservative static threshold (0.9) for canary; expose adaptive threshold that lowers when probe overhead measured below 0.5ms
Fallback choices: prefer quantized 4-bit model variant on same node group for low latency fallback; if unavailable, route to slow dedicated pool with circuit-breaker
Kernel-awareness: include kernel fingerprint in probe telemetry so router can prefer kernels with faster prefill-to-decode transition
Data retention: store probe traces for 7 days in hot bucket and aggregated metrics for 90 days for regression detection
tests: Unit: deterministic probe sampler/selector, scoring math, and circuit-breaker state transitions
Integration: end-to-end canary with 5% traffic on staging region with synthetic load profile (short/long mixed)
A/B: traffic-split experiment comparing baseline decode vs. speculative path measuring P95 latency, tokens per request, and quality (BLEU/ROUGE/semantic sim) on eval set
Chaos: inject model-variant failures and kernel launch delays to validate automatic fallback and rollout abort
updates: 2025-02-14 Asha Patel: Created ticket. Put together initial design doc and synthetic prompt set. Hypothesis: small, deterministic probe can identify fast-path viability for ~60% short queries.

2025-02-18 Liam Nguyen: Spike completed — implemented sampler + simple KL-based acceptance heuristic. Local staging run shows 0.6ms median overhead with naive batching; need kernel-aware optimization to reach target.
2025-02-21 Design review (Rosa Martinez): Requested clearer UX for Console toggles and a fallback user-visible metric. Also asked to surface per-route acceptance to debug regressions.
2025-02-24 PM feedback (Ethan Clarke): Prioritize safety — default canary at 1% with automatic rollback when early-divergence rate > 1% over 10m. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-27 Eng sync: Decided to use EWMA(α=0.2) for acceptance history smoothing and to include kernel fingerprint in probe trace. Trade-off: slightly higher metadata costs for better routing decisions.

2025-03-01 Liam Nguyen: Prototype PR opened (link above). End-to-end canary scheduled in staging. Observed one failure mode where cache warmup from probe evicts expensive KV entries — mitigated by deterministic sample selection (hash-based) and marking probe tokens as non-cacheable.

2025-03-03 Ops runbook draft: Added abort criteria (P95 latency regression > 10% or early-divergence > 2%) and steps to force-disable speculative routing globally via Console toggle. Assigned on-call rollback owner to SRE rotation.

2025-03-04 Next steps: Finalize dashboard panels, add A/B harness for quality metrics, and run 48h canary in eu-west-1 with 2% traffic. Follow-up ticket for long-term storage of probe traces will be created (ENG-XXX).
